sections.h2: What towns and landmarks make up Greene County?
sections.html:
Greene County occupies Georgia's east central Lake country, with Greensboro as both seat and biggest city. Lawmakers formed it on February 3, 1786 out of Washington County land, and it was named after Nathanael Greene, a major general in the Revolution (Wikipedia).

Of 406 square miles in total, 387 are land and 19, or 4.6%, are water. Streams drain three ways: the Oconee River across the west, the Little River toward the Savannah in the north, and the Ogeechee in the south. Oconee National Forest land reaches into the county, and the extinct river town of Scull Shoals recalls the county's earlier years. Interstate 20 runs through, with US 278 and State Routes 12, 15, 44 and 77 as other main roads.

The incorporated places are Greensboro, Union Point, White Plains, Woodville and the town of Siloam, and Bairdstown is an unincorporated community. Oglethorpe, Taliaferro, Hancock, Putnam, Morgan and Oconee counties ring it. Local families can choose among the Greene County School Board, Lake Oconee Academy and Nathanael Greene Academy. Whether a house is lakeside or in town, the bill comes from the tax commissioner's office.

sections.h2: How have Greene County's population and housing changed?
sections.html:
The 2020 count found 18,915 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 21,367 is 13.0% higher. People aged 65 and up are 33.5% of the total, about one in three, which is why the senior exemptions further down reach many local owners. Wikipedia links recent growth to people moving to Reynolds Lake Oconee.

sections.h2: Which Greene County office answers which tax question?
sections.html:
Both offices share one address on Silver Drive in Greensboro. Billing and collection fall to the commissioner, who covers real and personal property, mobile homes, vehicles, timber and utilities and also issues vehicle tags for the state. Values, returns and exemption approvals sit with the tax assessors.

  • Tax Commissioner: Suite 101 at 1034 Silver Drive, Greensboro, GA 30642, phone 706-453-3358, lobby open Monday through Friday, 8:00 to 4:45.
  • Tax Assessors: Suite 102 in the same building, phone 706-453-3355, for values, appeals and homestead filings.
  • Online: the county site carries a homestead application page and a page on the yearly digest and assessments.

Hours and forms are posted on the commissioner's page and the assessors' appeal page.

sections.h2: When does Greene County expect payment?
sections.html:
December 1 is the county's due date. If it falls on a weekend or holiday, payment is due the following business day. The commissioner's page warns that a parcel with tax left unpaid can eventually be seized and sold.

Other dates follow a set pattern. Returns cover property held on January 1 and run through April 1. A real property return carries forward at the earlier value, whereas personal property needs a new return each year. For mobile homes the state's county facts sheet says the owner returns the home for tax by April 1 and applies for the yearly location permit between January 1 and April 1. Assessment notices tend to go out around May, and the commissioners and the school board set millage rates later in the year.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Greene County assessment?
sections.html:
The clock runs 45 days from the mailing date. Grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, and the appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors on the state's uniform form, PT-311A. Your first filing must name the route you choose.

  • Equalization route: the assessors review first and can send a corrected notice, which you may contest within 30 days; anything left unchanged goes to a hearing before the Board of Equalization, with Superior Court as the last step.
  • Hearing officer: value disputes over non-homestead real property of $1,000,000 or more may go to a certified appraiser.
  • Arbitration: file with a current certified appraisal. If the assessors reject it, the clerk of Superior Court receives the case, a hearing is held within 30 days, and the arbitrator's decision ends the matter.

The county page describes each route in more detail and says forms are online at the state revenue department.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Greene County use?
sections.html:
To qualify for a given year you must own and occupy the home on January 1 and file by April 1, since later filings roll to the next year. After approval it renews itself until ownership, residence or exemption type changes. The county's chart lists these deductions from assessed value:

  • S1, the state default: $2,000, applied to county and school taxes.
  • L1, age 65 and over: $10,000, described as $2,000 state plus $8,000 local.
  • S3, ages 62 to 64, net income capped at $10,000: $2,000 on county taxes and $10,000 on school taxes.
  • L4, age 65 and over, net income capped at $10,000: $12,000 on county taxes and $18,000 on school taxes.
  • S5 and L5, a 100% disabled veteran or unremarried surviving spouse: $100,896, a 2021 state figure that changes annually and needs proof.

A trailing F on a code, as in S1F, flags the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value since the day the exemption was approved. Per the county, the freeze reaches the home and as many as five acres, but excludes pools, barns, detached garages and shops (county homestead page). A deferral program lets owners aged 62 or older put off, though not erase, tax when household income is no more than $15,000, and qualifying farmland can be assessed at 30%.

sections.h2: What should a Greene County seller do about tax before closing?
sections.html:
The state revenue department states that a January 1 owner remains liable for the full year, even after a January 2 sale, and no refund is paid for a partial year. The purchase contract normally splits the bill, so what counts is the exact balance on the parcel.

Ask the commissioner's office for a written statement of tax owed for this year and any earlier ones. If the sale falls close to December 1, ask which amount the closing agent should send. Keep the assessment notice and any appeal paperwork in the file, since a pending appeal can alter the final bill. Tell the assessors in writing when you move out, so your homestead code comes off the property and the next owner can apply in their name.

faqs.q: Which day is Greene County property tax due?
faqs.a: December 1, rolling to the next business day when it falls on a weekend or holiday. The commissioner's page adds that a parcel with unpaid tax may be levied upon and eventually sold.

faqs.q: How much time do I have to dispute a Greene County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the mailing date of your assessment notice. Send a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors that names your route: Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitration.

faqs.q: By what date must I file Greene County homestead paperwork?
faqs.a: April 1 for the current tax year. You need to have owned the home and lived in it on January 1, and an application filed afterward applies the next year.

faqs.q: What does the code S1F mean on a Greene County notice?
faqs.a: The F marks the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value above the level on the day your homestead was approved. The county says it reaches the house and up to five acres, and leaves out pools, barns, detached garages and shops.

faqs.q: Which Greene County office do I phone about a bill or a value?
faqs.a: Call the tax commissioner at 706-453-3358 about bills and payments, and the tax assessors at 706-453-3355 about values, appeals and exemptions. Both work from 1034 Silver Drive in Greensboro.
